issues.title: Initial Discussion Notes
issues.author: johngray-dev
issues.body:
Here is combined notes from Mike Ounsworths and myself:


Attendees: John Gray, Luke (NCSC), DavidBen, Bas, Jan Klaußner


David:  https://www.chromium.org/Home/chromium-security/post-quantum-auth-roadmap/

Discussion on Use Cases:

High volume (batching)
- Batch signing, if you're concerned about HSM capacity

High auditability
- PKIs that issue admin credentials?
- A more efficient and flexible transparency/auditing scheme, if you either already use CT or would have found auditing schemes compelling if CT worked differently 
- Auditing case, private PKI's audited to the hilt.   Work by dumping something out of a database.  Extra machinery is worth it if you don't trust the operator of the PKI. 
- System of building trusting... Can trust be reduced to automation.

Allowing things to stay on RSA / ECC
- Imagine an industrial IoT setting where things want to continue using ECDSA certs for size reasons. Imagine putting those into an MTC and having a witness that monitors for suspicious activity adjacent to the closed IoT network continuing to use the legacy certs.

Use Case for Transport / Admin PKI
- Admin plane won't be high volume, but it needs to be high assurance.  Secret admin credential

Downgrade protection (using transparency logs)
- Have to turn off quantum vulnerable algorithms but still service quantum vulnerable certs.   Leads to a downgrade...
- Quantum capable client, server has both quantum and non-quantum...  Way to solve this in 2 ways.  HSTS is one way to fix.
- Second way is to use transparency auditing - then you can check by using the log
https://westerbaan.name/~bas/rwpqc2026/bas.pdf

Multiple co-signers
- Basically anything that uses Timestamp Authorities (RFC3161) today could map to this.
- eIDAS and ICAO ePassport

PQC Migration:
- Possible use of migration?   Downgrade attacks?   CA service provider.  
- Way to get web PKI off classic roots

eIDAS - ICAO (passports)
- Jan mentioned this as a use-case

Landmark build-up:
- Imagine a smartcard building access door reader. It needs to be able to accept any employee ID badge issued in the past 10 years. This device will have limited on-board memory. Today, it has the root cert, and just needs to fetch today’s CRL (then throw out yesterday’s CRL). This use case wants MTC to have a landmark scheme where the new landmark replaces the previous landmark.
- We should provide guidance for how to calculate the bound (ceiling) on how much disk space is required for a Verifier to successfully be able to validate all certificates issued in a X day window.

Landmark build-up:
- Imagine a smartcard building access door reader. It needs to be able to accept any employee ID badge issued in the past 10 years. This device will have limited on-board memory. Today, it has the root cert, and just needs to fetch today’s CRL (then throw out yesterday’s CRL). This use case wants MTC to have a landmark scheme where the new landmark replaces the previous landmark.
- We should provide guidance for how to calculate the bound (ceiling) on how much disk space is required for a Verifier to successfully be able to validate all certificates issued in a X day window.


General
- Timestamp authority, counter-signer - anything that uses TSA's could be a target for multi-signed MTC
- The landmark certificates optimization, if (a subset of) your RPs are able to manage it
- Might be use-cases without connection to update service..  Has access to a mechanism to fetch landmarks.
- Server could send landmarks to client if they don't have them.
- Longer cert lifetimes - client will have to store more landmarks.   
- Create a scheme for rebasing the landmarks?  
- How to re-anchor the card once it is out.
- Can we make a MT of the landmarks?
- Need a fetching mechanism - like CRL's
- There is a fall back mode...  
- What are the options for making use of this new tool, and what is the advantages
- Zero trust work-from-home, continuous authentication - new VPN connection every so often.

- Rebase only if you are not happy with the rebase - maybe tuning parameters
- You need to allocate this much disk space -  10 years * 365 landmarks * 32


John / Bas Conversations (April 22nd, 2026)
- Maybe we start simple - a Certificate Verifier for clients which use the MTC landmarks.   Non web PKI's will likely come across MTC and need to know how to verify.
- A mechanism to fetch landmarks (could be like a CRL mechanism).   Maybe an LDP (Landmark Distribution point)? 
- a new purpose intent for draft-lamps-certificate-discovery?  Or just define separately

issues.title: Clarify signed-artifact verification horizons beyond batch tree-head retention
issues.author: VeriCommons
issues.body:
In [draft-ietf-plants-mtc-deploy-use-cases-00, Section 3.5.5](https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-plants-mtc-deploy-use-cases-00.txt),
signed artifacts may require verification throughout their operational
lifetime, while the minimum batch-tree-head retention duration is based on
the maximum certificate validity period in the corresponding batch.

Could the section also connect an application's intended verification horizon
to its required verification inputs and the parties responsible for retaining
them? The existing requirement for continued access after CA decommissioning
would remain unchanged.

Consider an application evaluating in 2045 a signature made in 2028. All
published batch tree heads remain accessible, but the application policy
requires an authenticated OCSP response retained to support the certificate-status
determination at the relevant historical time. If that response is lost and
no equivalent evidence is available from a source accepted by the policy,
retaining the batch tree heads cannot recover the missing status evidence.

This issue concerns application validation inputs beyond the MTC certification
proof. With the relying party's configured, trusted cosigner parameters and
cosigner policy available, a standalone MTC can authenticate its subtree
without fetching an external tree head. That does not supply every historical
validation input required by the application. Historical validation is also
distinct from accepting an expired certificate for a current operation.
See [MTC-07, Sections 6.3 and 7.1–7.2](https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-plants-merkle-tree-certs-07.html#section-6.3).

Suggested text after the existing Section 3.5.5 paragraph:

> Where an application's intended verification horizon extends beyond this
> minimum period, its archival policy should identify the required verification
> inputs, their retention periods, and the parties responsible for preserving
> and making them available. These inputs depend on the certificate
> representation and application validation policy; retained batch tree heads
> alone need not be sufficient. The policy should provide for continuity of
> those responsibilities when an issuer or archive service is retired. This
> guidance does not extend certificate validity or change certificate validation
> requirements.

The clarification does not allocate MTC syntax or an archival container, and
does not prescribe one historical-validation policy. Existing evidence-record
formats and application profiles retain their roles. Its applicability to
long-lived document signatures is motivation, not a request to add a document
format to this deployment draft.

pulls.title: Jg landmark subtrees
pulls.author: johngray-dev
pulls.body: Add text about possible landmark format and landmark consistency proof structure.

comments.body: If we think of landmarks as just special subtrees of the Merkle Tree, can you use the Subtree Consistency Proofs in section 4.4?

Should we start with maybe a simpler case of trying to send down a list of landmarks, but without wanting to send the signatures for all of the landmarks.

some alternative text maybe:  

A verifier requesting updated landmarks may require a lot of new landmarks. 
Requiring the verifier to retrieve and validate every intermediate
landmark individually would increase both network traffic and signature
verification costs.

...

With the Landmark proofs you could just have the proof from one landmark to the next, keeping them in a chain. 

Then later on, the retrieval mechanism would be for the verifier to send the point on the tree they want the list to start from, this could be their most up to date point on the tree in their cache so far. 

~~~
LandmarkDistributionPoint?
start=<start_tree_size>&
end=<end_tree_size>
~~~

and the response would be all the landmarks from the start, with the landmark proofs between them, finishing at the final landmark and the signature material for that final landmark! 


Sorry for the lateness of the comment before the deadline - hopefully this all makes sense
